advances: An exact all-parameter path in the reflected-core class with the original mixed measure. The payment uses the two selected isolating menus.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Let $h_z(n)$ be the support function of the old ambient hull's real fiber above $z\in[0,3]$. It is concave in $z$ for fixed $n$, since any combination of support maximizers is in the corresponding intermediate fiber. Define
$$
\Phi_A(n,z,x)=[n\cdot(x-c_A)-B_Az]_+,\qquad
\Phi_C(n,z,x)=[n\cdot(x-c_C)+B_C(z-3)]_+,\qquad
\Phi=\Phi_A+\Phi_C .
$$
Choose the positive constants large enough that each summand vanishes on the three other old compact sampled fibers, uniformly in $n$. On its own paying boundary, each equals $n\cdot(x-c)$ for the corresponding $c$, because this support is positive. The divergence theorem gives integral $da$ on either own boundary, including the two-endpoint form for $d=1$. Each menu captures the whole of its paying endpoint and none of the other endpoint. Its numerator is therefore $da$ and the common denominator $2da$ for every indicated weighting.

For $z\in[0,3]$ take all inequalities $n\cdot x+\epsilon\Phi(n,z,x)\le h_z(n)$. They are convex constraints, and their nonnegative fields imply containment in the original hull. The intersection is closed because the equivalent affine-majorant support description of each upper polyhedral support graph in $z$ gives closed inequalities. Indeed, at a fixed $n$, $h_z(n)$ is the upper roof of the four points $(j,h_j(n))$, as follows by using the hull's base representations. Both old middle bodies satisfy all their cuts with equality of the allowable fiber, since $\Phi=0$ on them. At an endpoint translate $x$ by its center $c$. Every point in the new fiber lies in the old one, so the other field vanishes, and the local inequalities are $n\cdot(x-c)+\epsilon[n\cdot(x-c)]_+\le h_{K_p-c}(n)$. The right side is positive. This is equivalent to $n\cdot(x-c)\le h_{K_p-c}(n)/(1+\epsilon)$, giving the exact homothet. The old strict full and empty cap statuses persist on these subsets, and all four fibers stay positive. In particular the projection stays $[0,3]$.

Both endpoint homothets lie in the original reflected core and have volume $a_\epsilon$. Apply the exact depth theorem to obtain $Q_\epsilon=q+a_\epsilon$ and $M_\epsilon=2(V+a_\epsilon)$. The ratio is increasing as a function of $a_\epsilon$ since its derivative with respect to that volume is $(V-q)/(2(V+a_\epsilon)^2)>0$, using $q\le V/2$. The stated time derivative follows from $a'_0=-da$.

For the planar calibration the centroid is $g=(1/3,1/3)$ and $V=1/2$. The centroid bound 6769574fc1bd9f8d gives depth at least $2/9$ there. The three caps where one of the three barycentric coordinates is at least $1/3$ have area $(2/3)^2V=2/9$ each, and cover the whole triangle because the coordinates sum to one. Hence $q=2/9$. The reflected core is given by $0\le x_1,x_2\le2/3$ and $1/3\le x_1+x_2\le1$. For $A$ the sums range from $29/60$ to $41/60$, and for $C$ from $85/120$ to $115/120$. Each coordinate interval lies strictly inside $(0,2/3)$, so the two bodies and their reflections are strictly inside $K$. Their areas both equal $1/100$. Their first-coordinate centroid values are $1/4$ and $1/2$, with both middle values $1/3$, giving the nonaffine centroid graph. The first-coordinate intervals exclude $1/3$ at both endpoints. The largest fiber volume is $1/2<51/100$, and the middle deepest bases have opposite parity. Substitution gives the stated rational values, and $a_\epsilon\to0$ gives the limit.
statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be a compact convex body with volume $V$, ordinary deepest mark $g$ and raw ordinary maximum $q$. Place two copies of $K$ at bases $1,2$ and compact convex bodies $A,C\subset K\cap(2g-K)$ of equal volume $a>0$ at bases $0,3$. Use the two critical menus obtained by extending a positive balanced ordinary critical circuit at $g$ by common sufficiently large negative base tilt about $1$ and positive base tilt about $2$, respectively, with any probability weights in each. For arbitrary interior points $c_A,c_C$ of the endpoint bodies, one nonnegative jointly continuous field convex in the full physical coordinates at each unit normal pays efficiency exactly $1/2$ against both old boundary profiles. Its convex support cuts yield, for every $\epsilon\ge0$, endpoint homothets of ratio $(1+\epsilon)^{-1}$ about $c_A,c_C$, with both middle fibers fixed. Put $a_\epsilon=a/(1+\epsilon)^d$. The actual normalized maximum is $(q+a_\epsilon)/(2(V+a_\epsilon))$, strictly decreases, and has right derivative $-da(V-q)/(2(V+a)^2)$ at zero.

For $K=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}$ and the endpoints
$$
A=[1/5,3/10]\times[17/60,23/60],\qquad
C=[2/5,3/5]\times[37/120,43/120],
$$
the centroid of $K$ is outside both endpoints, the four fiber centroids are nonaffine in the base, and all four fibers weigh strictly less than half the total mass. There are exactly two deepest marks, at opposite base parities. The original values are $Q=209/900$, $M=51/50$, $\beta=209/918=2/9+5/918$, and the exact path has $\beta\downarrow2/9$.
title: An exact simultaneous endpoint contraction with decreasing normalized depth
